name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Indonesia's rupiah trades near record lows above 18,200 per dollar, down about 8% this year; no EM default or IMF rescue
state: The rupiah weakened to about 18,275 per dollar on 19 Nov (Katadata Databoks), after a record low of 18,250 on 12 Nov driven by a strong dollar, expected Fed rate rises and domestic political uncertainty (Jakarta Post). Bisnis reported on 19 Nov that the rupiah had fallen 8.4% in 2026, with Bank Indonesia pointing to global conditions. The fall is gradual, well short of 10% in a month, and no major emerging economy in default, imposing capital controls or seeking emergency IMF support was found as of 28 Nov, so the level stays Normal.
for_you: Indonesian importers, firms with dollar debts and holders of rupiah assets are most exposed. Sharp emerging-market currency falls tend to raise local inflation and borrowing costs in the countries affected.
rubric_hit: Normal: no major EM currency down >10% in a month, default, capital controls or emergency IMF request (rupiah −8.4% in 2026)

sources.title: Katadata Databoks — Rupiah Exchange Rate Weakens to IDR 18,275 per US Dollar (19 November 2026)

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
